verdicts.note: Self-identifies as female ('being a female') throughout; clear.
'a mixed comprehensive school' directly = mixed sex.
'doing manufacturing and design management', started mechanical then swapped; fits Mech & Manufacturing.
Quote evidences interest in maths/physics more than 'good at'; did Maths/Physics A-levels so plausible, but downgrade.
'I quite like knowing how things are made' + 'stretches your brain' supports interesting work.
'it's all about problem solving' directly supports challenge of solving problems.
'it's quite a big area ... it's like vast' supports varied appeal.
'my dad's an engineer' = family member in industry; clear.
Garage play is framed as father's stuff/childhood, not her own established technical hobbies; thin, downgrade.
'not in the sense that you're going to do engineering ... He wasn't like that' supports father did not actively encourage = disagree.
Advisor helped with university choice, not encouraging engineering specifically = disagree.
School product design + engineer father + gap year = chose with substantial knowledge, so disagree with 'little knowledge'.
Asked why not going on placement; 'I just wanted to graduate' = not going = no.
Substantial prior work experience; interviewer confirm 'if you hadn't done a year out' -> 'Yes definitely' links it to not going.
'wait another year and probably get paid better ... just wanted to graduate' supports finishing sooner to earn.
'doing like more like research or R & D kind of stuff' explicitly names R&D as preferred specialization.
'I would like to do like manager' + enjoys project management supports managerial.
Interviewer offered 'pay or training'; she picked training and elaborated, genuine but partly led, downgrade.
Prompted by 'would you like to travel' but gives substantive enthusiastic own reasons (different countries, send back to UK).
'location I suppose, money ...' - hedged passing mention in a list; weak but lists it as a factor; confidence already low.
About managers listening/caring; relates to people worked with mattering. Reasonable fit.
Asked re career choices generally; 'happy how I've ended up' + 'can't imagine not doing what I've done' covers pleased with studying engineering.

Quote is about prior mechanical course modules not used in gap year, not relevance-comprehension on current course; underlying sentiment ('stupid lectures', modules not useful) present but loose, downgrade.
Wanted more 'make stuff' which they haven't done = level of practical work not just right = disagree.
Clear disappointment at lack of hands-on/lathe work supports dissatisfied with practical work.
Praises manufacturing lectures (her main lectures) as best thing = satisfied; some criticism of science being basic but net positive.
'generally bad ones ... quite stressful' + finds working with the women hard = dissatisfied.
